newsitem.title: USA: Cool weather to follow warm spell in central U.S.
newsitem.headline: Cool weather to follow warm spell in central U.S.

text.p: U.S. winter wheat and livestock in the central United States should be aided by milder weather the next week or so, meteorologists said.

Warm weather, with temperatures nearing 70 degrees Fahrenheit, was forecast for Kansas to Texas through the weekend. That same system should raise temperatures to the upper 40s in the southern Midwest this weekend and upper 30s in the northern Midwest.
The warm weather will be replaced by cooler weather by the middle of next week but meteorologists said the cold should be about normal for the season.
Forecasts varied regarding rainfall next week in the hard red winter wheat areas of Kansas to Texas.
Weather Services Corp's Joel Burgio expects light rain of 0.1 inch or less from Texas to eastern Kansas.
Tim Bowden, Weather Express Inc meteorologist, expects more rain, possibly 0.1 to 0.5 inch from the Texas Panhandle to southwest Kansas and up to 0.75 inch in southeast Kansas.

Both meteorologists have the storm system moving into the Midwest next week bringing rain to the southern areas and possibly snow to the north. Equivalent moisture amounts may range from 0.25 to 1.00 inch.

The Pacific Northwest continued to receive rain, with 1.0 to 2.5 inches falling the past 24 hours in southern Washington and Oregon, Burgio said. Up to 0.5 inch was forecast Friday and another 0.25 inch Saturday.
After Sunday, clear weather was forecast for much of next week for that region.
